name: CDOT
chain: CDOT S-Standard Plans, S-630 series (July 2026 re-issue — editorial only per CDOT issuance memo)

sign_spacing.note: Key to Advance Signing Distances: A=B=C=100 on urban <=40 mph. A=B=C on surface streets is the national convention (Table 6B-1), not a CDOT collapse.
CDOT draws the urban low/high-speed breakpoint at 40/45; the cities draw it at 30/35 — both lawful (Table 6B-1 delegates it to the agency).
A=1000, B=1500, C=2640 — the progression is retained only on expressways/freeways.

device_spacing.rule: Tapers/transitions: spacing = speed limit in feet. Tangents: max 2x speed (General Note 18).

buffer.rule: 'Buffer space is optional' — site-specific, per the Engineer (General Note 24). CDOT's speed-keyed buffer values are more permissive than the national Table 6B-2 at high speed (650' @ 75 vs national 820'; 570' @ 65 vs 645') — jurisdiction-aware lookup required.

other.rule: Termination taper = 100 ft (S-630-5, which also independently reprints the taper formulas L=WS >=45 / WS²/60 <45 and the same A/B/C table).
Speed reduction per CDOT Form 568; max 15 mph reduction per sign installation; Work Zone (G20-5p) + Fines Double (R2-6p) every 2640 ft (General Notes 3/4).
Portable rumble strips placed within the advance-warning sign series; work zones <=75 mph only (S-630-5).

geometry.note: Status: CONTRACT + PERMIT TERMS — not law absent a CDOT contract or permit. S-630-1 (19 sheets, ~26 typical-application layouts) is THE drawing-conventions reference.

deltas.rule: Congestion beyond the sign sequence -> add advance signing beyond it (General Note 11).

trigger.condition: congestion extends beyond the advance sign sequence

deltas.rule: ADA: construction impacting ramps at more than one crossing -> temporary ADA ramps SHALL be installed (detail per DS-630-2a); ped signal faces on closed crosswalks covered; temporary ped facilities shall replicate features of the existing facility; bypass adjacent to an open traffic lane -> concrete barrier protection; channelizing devices plastic or concrete with a compliant detectable edge.

hours.override_note: No statewide published work-hour windows; hours are set per contract/permit (Form 568 and project special provisions).

personnel.rule: Spec 630.11: certified worksite traffic supervisor with current flagger cert required.
Approved TCS certification vendors: ATSSA (80% exam, 4,000 field hrs, 4-yr recert), CCA (2,000 hrs, 3-yr), WCCA (2,000 hrs, 3-yr), NSC (2-yr).

devices.rule: Cones >=28 in. SHALL be 36 in on freeways/expressways or nighttime. 'Should also be 36 inches' (guidance, not standard) on other high-speed roads: >=45 mph AND ADT >=6,000 (General Note 15).

trigger.condition: 36-in mandatory: freeway/expressway or night; 36-in guidance: >=45 mph AND ADT >=6,000

devices.rule: Type 1 barricades prohibited on 55 mph+ roadways (General Note 16). Type 3 barricades must be crash-tested (S-630-2).
VMS: consider >=1 mile in advance for interstate/high-speed lane closures (General Note 25).

notes.rule: CDOT rules bind as contract or permit terms (Special Use / Access permits), not as law absent one. Rolling roadblocks (S-630-7): minimum 4 law-enforcement vehicles upstream, TMA + VMS required — the spec if that scenario ever ships.

Work on state highways inside city limits requires a permit from EACH agency (the multi-agency answer is BOTH, not either/or — Colorado Springs Gen. Req. #20 states it concretely; Englewood/Wheat Ridge name specific CDOT roads).

fees.note: CDOT permit fees not researched (axis NC) — nothing encoded.

items.rule: Permit, insurance certificate(s), and traffic control plan must be available on site during work (Special Use Permit conditions).

source.doc: CDOT Special Use Permit conditions (incidental corroboration, Ingestion #30)
